step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents a serverless compute grid at DBS Bank used for pricing exotic option trades. Input data and job requests enter via an API Gateway. API Gateway writes non-sensitive input data to S3 (INPUT) and sends notifications to Amazon SNS. SNS fans out messages to three separate SQS queues representing different priority tiers: SQS (HIGH) for traders, SQS (MED) for back-office users, and SQS (LOW) for batch jobs. Each queue triggers dedicated AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency configured for each tier (300, 200, and 100 respectively) to ensure quality of service. EFS (BINARY) is mounted to the Lambdas to supply financial model binaries and eliminate cold starts. The outputs and function execution statuses are stored in DynamoDB, while execution logs are aggregated into Elasticsearch (OpenSearch) for end-to-end task monitoring.
